text:
Cheryl Hartman honored for teaching and leadership at University of South Dakota
Cheryl Hartman, a senior lecturer at the University of South Dakota’s Sioux Falls campus, was recognized on July 8 for her contributions to teaching and student engagement. Hartman, who earned her Master of Arts in English as the first woman in her family to obtain a graduate degree, later completed a Ph.D. in sociology before returning to USD as faculty.
Hartman currently serves as the sociology coordinator in the Department of Anthropology & Sociology. She said her experience at USD has been shaped by intellectually engaging courses, opportunities to lead classes as a teaching assistant, and lasting friendships formed during her studies. “I earned my M.A. in English, the first woman in my family to earn a graduate degree,” said Hartman.
Hartman highlighted the unique character of students at USD’s Sioux Falls campus: “The students bring life to the classroom,” she said. “Many are working adults, and some even have families. It is rewarding to see students grow from being unsure if college is right for them to becoming active, engaged, confident students who encourage each other.” She added that once students learn what sociology entails, they are eager to engage with course material: “I find great meaning in the work done at USD as we develop students to thrive in an ever-changing society.”
Beyond classroom instruction, Hartman has contributed by helping develop an accelerated program, supervising the Sociology Club, and supporting initiatives such as expanding USD’s student-run food pantry into Sioux Falls. Her leadership has enabled sociology students on campus to participate in projects with real-world impact.
Hartman's achievements include being named Professor of the Game at a 2024 basketball game and receiving both the Belbas-Larson Award for Excellence in Teaching (2026) and Johnson Family Outstanding Instructor Award (2025). She also completed USD’s President’s Executive Leadership Institute.
Reflecting on her journey from student to faculty member at USD, Hartman said: “Having been a student at USD and now being on the faculty means I have a heart for working at this university... I am extremely proud to say I work at USD. It has been the high point of my career.” She added that having an office where colleagues can drop by contributes greatly to feeling at home: “The cordial interactions and support from faculty, staff and students make me feel I belong.”
The Department of Sustainability and Environment operates within USD's College of Arts and Sciences; it uses Akeley-Lawrence Science Center as its main facility; it is unique regionally for offering both undergraduate and graduate degrees in sustainability; it promotes well-being through action locally; inspires positive change; extends influence via Missouri River Institute along Missouri National Recreational River, according to the official website.
